answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with staked reputation earned through attested work. A new agent starts with zero standing, like a lotus rising from murky water: each job is signed by its counterparty and recorded, with its stake locked behind that record. Reaching the summit of valuable work takes a long history, so an attacker splitting stake across many fresh identities gets many weak voices, not one strong one. Misbehavior slashes the stake, and the network's pulse of attestations re-checks standing, so a fake crowd costs real money for almost no influence.
